terra.problem: Saying Israel had a front-row seat but the LORD did the fighting suggests Israel only watched. Joshua also speaks of an Israelite putting a thousand to flight (Joshua 23:10).
The explanation repeats the verse and lists its parts without much of Papa Dorin's warmth or personality.
The kitchen comparison is generic, and the rest simply repeats that rebuilding is not mentioned.
Calling Eleazar a priest states a fact from outside this passage without a reference.
Saying the whole speech is about land overstates it. Joshua also speaks about obeying the Law and holding fast to the LORD.
It assigns Joshua an unstated purpose: that he piles up the pictures so the listeners cannot miss them.
It says the warning is meant to be uncomfortable, assigning an intention the text does not state.
It says Joshua repeats himself so nobody misses it, but the text does not give that reason.
‘Whatever the LORD says, comes to pass’ makes a broader claim than Joshua's statement about the promises and calamity addressed in this passage.
